extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, Patent Office officials, and judges considering appeals from the Commissioner of Patents
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing appeals from the Commissioner of Patents (jurisdiction, scope of review, remedies) and the Patent Office rules for taking/transmitting evidence in contested/interference proceedings under the 1836 and 1839 Acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By the sixth section of the act, the applicant must be the inventor; one of several joint inventors cannot properly be called the inventor, and if he applies the Commissioner is bound to refuse the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner has authority to withhold a patent from an applicant who is not the sole inventor. The question whether an applicant is sole inventor is material irrespective of whether the device is entirely new or an improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory public-use bar (two-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the machine was in public use for more than two years before application, the applicant may have lost his right to a patent (statutory language refers to 'public use' and bars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Cranch noted this ground in a prior opinion but later withdrew the extra-judicial part of that discussion because the appeal was confined to the reasons of appeal; the public-use bar is part of the statutory grounds but should be decided only when properly raised within the appeal's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability: only rejected applicants may appeal (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal to the judge is given to an applicant whose application has been rejected by the Commissioner; in general no appeal is provided from the granting of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general object of the appeal provisions is to correct the error of the Commissioner in refusing to grant a patent; erroneous grants are corrected by ordinary tribunals (actions at law or equity) rather than by this special appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited appellate scope: review confined to reasons of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge's revision is to be 'confined to the points involved in the reasons of appeal' and he is to hear and determine such appeals only as to those points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner did not err on the points in the reasons of appeal, his decision as to those points must be affirmed even if the judge thinks the patent ought to have been granted on the whole merits; conversely, if the judge reverses on those points, remaining untouched objections may permit the Commissioner to still refuse — the judge's decision governs only the portions involved in the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner must set forth written grounds of decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall lay before the judge all original papers and evidence in the case, together with the grounds of his decision, fully set forth in writing, touching all the points involved in the reasons of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This written statement is required by statute (e.g., section 11 of 1839) and frames the issues for the judge's confined review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's jurisdiction limited to contending applicants (sec. 8 construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 8th section, the judge is to determine which or whether either of the applicants is entitled to receive a patent as prayed for; his authority was designedly limited to contending applicants — not to decide between an applicant and an already existing patentee except as the statute expressly provides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patentee (one who already has a patent) is not an 'applicant' and generally has no right to appeal to this special tribunal; remedies for a patentee are by suit at law or equity (including section 16 interference suits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee's remedies after grant (limits of Commissioner's control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the patent has issued the Commissioner's jurisdiction is exhausted except in the case provided by section 13 (defective or insufficient description); an adjudication by the Commissioner or judge has no effect on an already granted patent as to the patentee's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a second patent is erroneously issued, the first patentee may vindicate his rights in equity (sec. 16) or at law; the special appeal procedure is primarily to aid disappointed applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of examiners review on request (sec. 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the specification and claim have not been so modified as, in the opinion of the Commissioner, shall entitle the applicant to a patent, the applicant may, on appeal and upon written request, have the decision of a board of examiners who may reverse the Commissioner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides an internal administrative review step where the Commissioner objects to the claim/specification as not properly modified to sustain a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for interfering applications/patents (sec. 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application would, in the opinion of the Commissioner, interfere with any other patent for which an application may be pending or with any unexpired patent, the Commissioner must give notice to such applicant or patentee and, if dissatisfied, he may appeal on like terms and conditions as provided for rejected applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judge's role under this section is to determine which (if either) of the contending applicants is entitled to receive a patent; this provision contemplates hearings on priority between contending applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's procedural rules for evidence — Rule 1 (writing and oath)
rubrics_metrics.description: All statements, declarations, evidence, etc., shall be in writing, setting forth minutely and particularly the point or points at issue; and shall be verified by oath or affirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Office requires written, sworn statements describing the issues specifically; unsworn or informal statements are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's procedural rules for evidence — Rule 2 (filing before hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: All statements, declarations, proofs, and evidence shall be filed in the Patent Office by the parties, respectively, before the day of hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence not filed before the hearing date is generally not to be considered unless compliance is excused under the limited exception(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's procedural rules for evidence — Rule 3 (notice of depositions and right to cross-examine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the deposition of a witness or witnesses be taken by either party, notice shall be given to the opposite party of the time and place when and where such deposition(s) will be taken, so that the opposite party, either in person or by attorney, shall have full opportunity to cross-examine the witness or witnesses; such notice, with proof of service, must be attached to the deposition whether the party cross-examines or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be given in sufficient time for appearance and for the transmission of the evidence to the Patent Office before the day of hearing; failure to provide sufficient notice may be a ground of objection though objections should generally be raised at trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's procedural rules for evidence — Rule 4 (no consideration of noncompliant evidence on hearing day)
rubrics_metrics.description: No evidence, statement, or declaration touching the matter at issue will be considered upon the day of hearing which shall not have been taken and filed in compliance with these rules: Provided, that if either party shall be unable, from good and sufficient reasons, to procure the testimony of a witness within the above time, he must give notice of the same to the Commissioner accompanied with statements of the cause of such inability (to be received some days previous to the day of hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule precludes last-minute informal transmissions from being considered at the scheduled hearing unless timely notice of inability and cause is shown; it is the basis for objecting to informally transmitted depositions but the Commissioner retained some discretion to postpone to further the ends of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's procedural rules for evidence — Rule 5 (sealing and certification of transmitted evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: All evidence shall be sealed up and transmitted to the Commissioner of Patents by the persons before whom it shall be taken, and so certified thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper transmission (sealed and certified by the officer taking the deposition) is required; evidence transmitted informally may be disregarded or may justify postponement to allow cure of the informality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's discretion to postpone hearing to further justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may postpone a scheduled hearing to enable cure of informality in transmission of evidence and to give both parties opportunity to procure further testimony, when in his judgment doing so furthers the public interest and the ends of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discretion is contestable (an appellant argued the Commissioner precluded himself by his own rules), but the Commissioner may postpone rather than rigidly enforce denial if the informality could be remedied and justice served by postponement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of judge's reversal on subsequent Commissioner proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the judge reverses the Commissioner upon the points involved in the reasons of appeal, the effect of that judgment upon further proceedings of the Commissioner depends on whether the reasons of appeal involved the merits of the whole case; the judge's decision governs only the points in the appeal and may leave other sufficient reasons untouched for the Commissioner to reject the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a new rejection based on untouched grounds would itself be subject to appeal is left open; the practical effect depends on whether the judge's affirmed or reversed points encompassed the substantive merits.
